Unlike standard ALC, which calculates the next step based on the current position and all available bounds, Sub-stepping physically advances the ray to validate bounds, ensuring that each additional level of detail contributes positively or neutrally to the step size [S1].

The claim states that Sub-stepping physically advances the ray to validate bounds, ensuring that each additional level of detail contributes positively or neutrally to the step size. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes the Sub-stepping algorithm: 'Our new algorithm works by safely making intermediate sub-steps along the ray as intermediate sums Fi are computed... Furthermore, the text states that this method 'guarantees that step*i*+1 ≥ step*i*', which corresponds to the claim that additional levels contribute positively or neutrally (non-decreasing) to the step size.

Specifically, Equation 15 defines $step_{i+1} = step_i + ...$, implying the new position is $t_{new} = t_{old} + step_{i+1}$. The claim implies a single calculation from the initial $t_0$ using a final step size, which contradicts the iterative, cumulative nature of the sub-stepping algorithm described in the text.
